extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents, transferees, and practitioners filing or managing Canadian patent applications (including PCT national phase entrants)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and substantive requirements for correcting applicant/inventor names/identities, recording transfers and name changes, registering related documents, and claiming/restoring priority for Canadian patent applications (including PCT national phase entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of applicant identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The person who submitted the application to obtain a filing date or for PCT national phase entry will be able to request the correction of the identity of the applicant, as long as the error arose from inadvertence, accident or mistake without any fraudulent or deceptive intention and the person who submitted the application provides a statement to that effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must include the relevant statement (see section 104 of the Patent Rules). Distinguish identity changes from mere name corrections. Time limits vary (see related time-limit metrics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for correction of applicant identity — regular Canadian application
rubrics_metrics.description: For a regularly filed application the request will have to be made before the earlier of when the application becomes open to public inspection and the day on which the Commissioner receives a request to record a transfer under section 49 of the Patent Act (section 104 of the Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit correction before public inspection or before a transfer recording request is received to be effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for correction of applicant identity — PCT national phase application
rubrics_metrics.description: For a PCT national phase application the request must be submitted before the earlier of (subsection 154(6) of the Patent Rules): the later of: three months from the date that the application enters national phase; and if the Commissioner sends a notice under subsection 154(7) before the end of the three months from entry, the day on which the three month period after the date of the notice expires; and the Commissioner receives a request to record a transfer under section 49 of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex deadline: calculate the later-of and earlier-of dates carefully; monitor notices under 154(7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of applicant name (no change in identity)
rubrics_metrics.description: An error in the naming of an applicant that does not result in a change of identity can be corrected by request from the applicant so long as it is submitted on or before the payment of the final fee, or if the final fee is refunded, on or before it is paid again. The request must also contain a statement to the effect that the correction does not add or delete the name of an applicant or change the identity of a named applicant (section 105 of the Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the required statement. The deadline ties to the final fee payment; ensure timing if fees are refunded and repaid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of request to correct applicant name/identity
rubrics_metrics.description: All requests for correction to the naming of an applicant in a patent application must comply with the requirements for submitting written communications to the Commissioner. Every request must include: application number; name of the applicant(s); a clear request for correction of an error of an identity or only the name; and any additional information that may be needed, such as the statement outlined in section 104, 105 or subsection 154(6) of the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Chapter 2 requirements for written communications. Be explicit about whether the correction changes identity or only corrects a name; include statutory statements where required to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of correction of an error in a patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: The correction of an error in a patent application will result in updating office records and the requester will be informed by letter that the correction has been made if requested by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office records are updated; request a confirmation letter if you require formal acknowledgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of naming of an inventor — identity vs name
rubrics_metrics.description: A correction of inventor identity is when the wrong person was identified in the application. A correction of name is meant to correct errors that do not change the identity (e.g., nickname vs formal name). The Office cannot always determine whether a correction changes identity or only the name; requesters should clearly note the type of correction. If the inventor is also an applicant, a separate request to correct an error in the naming of the applicant will need to be submitted. No fee is required for correcting an error in the naming of an inventor during the application stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state whether the change affects identity. Submit separate applicant corrections if applicable. No fee during application stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventor identity — timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An incorrectly identified inventor for a patent application can be corrected by request from the applicant if it is submitted before a notice of allowance or conditional notice of allowance is sent (section 106 of the Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure inventor identity corrections are made prior to allowance/conditional allowance notices to be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventor name (no change in identity) — timing and statement
rubrics_metrics.description: An error in the naming of an inventor in a patent application that does not result in a change of identity can be corrected by request from the applicant so long as it is submitted on or before the payment of the final fee, or if the final fee is refunded, on or before it is paid again. The request must also contain a statement to the effect that the correction does not add or delete the name of an inventor or change the identity of a named inventor (section 106 of the Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the statutory statement and meet the final-fee-linked deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of request to correct inventor name/identity
rubrics_metrics.description: All requests for corrections to the naming of an inventor in a patent application must comply with the requirements for submitting written communications to the Commissioner. Every request must include: application number; name of the applicant(s); any additional information that may be required, such as the statement outlined in paragraph 106(a) in the case of a correction that does not change the identity of the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Section 2.02.01 of Chapter 2 for formatting/submission requirements; include required statements to expedite processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of correction of inventor name/identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The correction of an error in a patent application will result in updating office records and the requester will be informed by letter that the correction has been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office updates records and can issue a letter on request; keep copy of correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear instructions and statutory references for transfers/changes
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to process the request correctly under the Patent Act and Patent Rules, applicants must clearly indicate what is being requested of the Commissioner and preferably indicate the section of the Patent Act or Patent Rules the office is to consider when processing your request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguous correspondence (e.g., simultaneously submitting transfer document + request to update records without specifying which relief is sought) will prompt the Office to request clarification, causing delays. Quote relevant sections to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording of transfer — limitations under section 49
rubrics_metrics.description: Although subsection 49(1) of the Patent Act states that the right or interest in an invention is transferable, section 49 does not provide for the recording of such transfers. If a request is submitted for the recording of a transfer of a right or interest in an invention to a person who is currently recorded as an applicant, the Office will notify the requestor that the transfer cannot be recorded under section 49. If submitted to a person not currently recorded as an applicant, the Office will notify that section 49 does not provide for the recording of rights or interest in an invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to use section 49 to record mere 'rights or interests' transfers; contact Office for correct mechanism. Refund of fees may be requested if request was incorrectly submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: International application transfers before national phase entry
rubrics_metrics.description: A transfer of an international application that took place before the national phase entry date in Canada is not considered to be a transfer of an application under section 49(2) of the Patent Act since an international application is considered to be an application for a patent filed in Canada beginning only on its national phase entry date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers prior to national phase entry are not recorded under section 49; requests to record such transfers will result in notification and possible fee refund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to record a transfer — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to record a transfer, the submission must contain (section 126 of the Patent Rules): the request to record the transfer; the name and the postal address of the transferee; and payment of the prescribed fee. All requests must comply with written communication requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure inclusion of transferee postal address and payment; follow Chapter 2 submission rules to avoid processing delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to record a transfer by applicant or patentee — evidence requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request to record a transfer is submitted by the applicant or the patentee, the Commissioner will record the transfer without additional required evidence (subsections 49(2) and (3) of the Patent Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the current recorded applicant/patentee requests recording, less documentary evidence is required; still comply with submission format and fee payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to record a transfer by the transferee — evidence examples
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request to record a transfer is submitted by the transferee (and not the currently recognized applicant or patentee), the transferee will need to provide evidence of the transfer. A copy of the document effecting the transfer along with one of the following would be considered satisfactory: a signed statement from the transferee that the document was signed/executed by all parties; an affidavit or other proof from a witness; the signature of a witness or corporate seal on the transfer document; or a document showing the transfer was registered in a patent office of another country. Requests and evidence will be placed on file and open to public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select at least one of the listed evidence types; be aware that evidence becomes public. See Chapter 5 for representation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording certificate issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the Commissioner has recorded the transfer, a certificate with a unique identification number will be sent to the person who requested the recording of the transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain the recording certificate as proof of the recorded transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of transfer recording — grounds and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner will remove the recording of the transfer of an application or a patent upon receipt of evidence satisfactory to the Commissioner that the transfer should not have been recorded. However, the Commissioner is not authorized to remove the recording of a transfer of a patent for the reason only that the transferor had previously transferred the patent to another person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide persuasive evidence if seeking removal; mere subsequent transfers by the transferor are not grounds for removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes of name (applicants) — general
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes of name that do not change the identity will be recognized on the request of the applicant or patentee. Changes of name are distinct and separate from the correction mechanisms for applicants under the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use section 125 for name changes (not correction procedures). If documentation affecting the patent exists, consider also registering related documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of name of applicant or patentee — Office position on scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office takes the position that section 125 of the Patent Rules applies only to a name change of a person who is currently recorded as an applicant or patentee in the records of the Office. The Office will not record a name change of a previously recorded applicant or patentee. Section 125 provides for recording the fact of a name change and does not provide for registration of related documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To record related documents, use section 124 registration separately. Ensure the person is currently recorded as applicant/patentee before seeking a name-change recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to record a name change — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to record a change of name, the submission must contain (section 125 of the Patent Rules): request to record the change of name; payment of the prescribed fee. All requests must comply with requirements for written communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Chapter 2 submission requirements and check Chapter 5 for who may represent the applicant in the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of a name change
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the Commissioner has recorded a change of name, a certificate with a unique identification number will be sent to the person who requested the change of name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the certificate as proof of recorded name change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of related documents — general distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may submit a request to the Commissioner to register a document relating to a patent application or patent (section 124 of the Patent Rules). Registration of a document is a separate mechanism than the recording of a transfer. Registration will put the document on file at the Patent Office but will not be treated as a request to record a transfer or change of name. Submission as an attachment to correspondence will place the related document on file and it will be available once the application is open to public inspection. A registration certificate or registration number will not be provided in that scenario.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose registration when you only want the document on file and not an amendment to chain of title; to effect chain-of-title changes, use recording mechanisms under sections 49/125/126 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to register a document — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to register a document, the submission must contain (section 124 of the Patent Rules): a request to register a document; the document to be registered; identification of the patent application or patent to which it relates (number); and payment of the prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the exact application/patent number; follow Chapter 2 for written communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of registration of a document
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the Commissioner has registered a document, a certificate with a unique identification number will be sent to the person who requested the registration of the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain the registration certificate for records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mergers affecting applicants — options for managing applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If a merger affecting an applicant for a patent occurs, clients may choose to: (1) do nothing; (2) request the recording of a transfer of the application or patent under section 49 of the Patent Act and section 126 of the Patent Rules (amendment to the chain of title); (3) request the recording of a name change under section 125 of the Patent Rules (amendment to the chain of title); or (4) request registration of a related document under section 124 of the Patent Rules (no amendment to the chain of title). The Office does not take a position as to whether a merger in fact transferred the rights or was simply a name change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the mechanism that matches the factual/legal effect of the merger; registering documents without recording transfers will not change chain of title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect your privacy on the Canadian Patents Database (CPD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to section 10 of the Patent Act most documents relating to a patent or patent application become available to the public once the application's confidentiality period has expired. Documents and information submitted effecting transfers or changes of names may contain sensitive personal information. CIPO will not publish these documents on the CPD, but they will be available to the public in person at the Office or upon request and payment of a prescribed fee. Submit only information needed as prescribed by the Patent Act and Rules. You may redact or suppress any information that you do not wish to be made public before you submit the document to CIPO, so long as this information is not required information according to the Patent Act and Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redact non-required personal information prior to submission; know that certain transfer/name-change documents will still be accessible on request (offline) even if not posted on CPD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting priority — where to make request and required information
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for priority must be made in the petition of the pending application or in another document other than the specification or drawings of the pending application. For each previously regularly filed application (a priority application), subsection 28.4(1) of the Patent Act and 73(1) of the Patent Rules require: the filing date; the name of the country or office of filing; and the number of the previously regularly filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not bury priority claims in the specification or drawings; provide filing date, country/office and application number for each priority application to be safe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — priority application number not known
rubrics_metrics.description: When the application number of the priority application is not known, the Patent Office will accept in place of the application filing number: a provisional number if any given by the office where filed; a copy of the request part of the previously filed application along with the date sent to the office; or a reference number given by the applicant and indicated in the previously filed application, along with the name and address of the applicant, the title of the invention and the date on which the application was sent to the office of filing (subsection 28.4(2.1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you lack the priority application number, provide one of the accepted alternatives and as much identifying information as possible to substantiate the priority claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period for the request for priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Under subsection 73(1) of the Patent Rules, an applicant may make a request for priority before the earlier of: the day after the date the applicant submits approval for the laying open to public inspection before the end of the confidentiality period, or the later of: the end of sixteen months after the earliest of the filing dates of the previously regularly filed applications (the priority applications); and four months after the filing date of the pending application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate both the 16-month and 4-month timelines and the public-inspection approval date to determine the earliest applicable deadline. Early public inspection approvals can shorten the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of priority information — priority filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: While it is possible to make corrections to the information required to make a request for priority, the time period to make these corrections can be very short. The Office strongly recommends that applicants ensure that the request is free from errors before submission. If there is an error in the filing date of the priority application, it may be corrected only if the applicant has not requested early public inspection before the end of the confidentiality period and if the correction request is submitted before the earliest deadline for making a request for priority when calculated using the uncorrected date and the corrected date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully compute deadlines using both original and corrected dates (see illustrative examples in the manual). Corrections may be denied if deadlines have passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of priority information — country/office or number
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible to request the correction of an error in the name of a country or office of filing and the number of the priority application under subsection 73(5) of the Patent Rules. The request must be submitted on or before payment of the final fee or if the final fee is refunded, on or before it is paid again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie corrections of country/office/number to the final-fee deadline; include required statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of priority application — requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant is required to provide a copy of each priority application for which they have made a request for priority under subsection 74(1) of the Patent Rules. This can be done by either: submitting a certified copy of the priority document and a certificate from the office of filing showing the filing date; or making a copy of the priority document available to the Commissioner in a digital library specified by the Commissioner, and informing the Commissioner of the access code (or the 4-digit confirmation number in the case of a USPTO application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide certified copies or use an accepted digital-access method and ensure the Commissioner can access the document (supply access code/confirmation number).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of submission of certified copy
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may submit a certified copy of the priority document and a certificate from the office of filing showing the filing date by all appropriate means set out in Chapter 2 of this manual (including all electronic means).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Chapter 2 methods for submission; electronic submission is acceptable where permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital library — WIPO Digital Access Service (DAS) accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Under specified Patent Rules provisions, the WIPO DAS is specified by the Commissioner as being accepted for making a copy of a previously filed application available to the Commissioner. Applicants may request that the office that has their priority document upload an electronic copy to DAS. Applicants who wish to upload a copy of a Canadian filed application or a PCT application filed with Canada as the receiving office may request CIPO to do so using the CIPO Order IP Documents web page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the priority document is uploaded to DAS and provide the access code; some offices auto-upload, others require applicant action. Use CIPO's form if you want CIPO to upload a Canadian/PCT document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — copy of priority application not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are not required to provide copies of priority documents under subsections 74(1) and (12) of the Patent Rules, under the following circumstances: the priority document is a Canadian application; the priority document is a PCT application filed in Canada as a receiving Office; or the pending application is a PCT national phase application and the applicant has complied with Rule 17.1(a), (b) or (b-bis) of the PCT Regulations in respect of the previously regularly filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether your priority document falls under an exception before omitting a copy; if unsure, provide the copy to avoid notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period to submit copy of priority documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who are required to submit or make available copies of priority documents must do so before the latest of: sixteen months after the earliest of the filing dates of the previously regularly filed applications; four months after the filing date of the pending application; and if the pending application is a PCT national phase application, the national phase entry date (subsection 74(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate the latest applicable date among the three listed; missing the deadline may trigger a notice from the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner’s notice to submit copy of priority documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant has not complied with the requirement to provide a copy of the priority document by the deadline, the Commissioner will send a notice to the applicant under subsection 74(4) requiring the applicant to do so not later than two months after the date of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly to the notice; the two-month compliance window is strict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional rule — applications filed before Oct 30, 2019
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed before October 30, 2019 that contain a compliant request for priority made before that date are not required to provide a copy of the priority application. If during examination the examiner takes into consideration the priority, they may require the applicant to submit a copy of the priority application by notice under subsection 196(1); the applicant must submit or make available a copy not later than four months after the date of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if exempt initially, you may be required to provide a copy later during examination; be prepared to comply within four months of a notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — copy of priority document not available (steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant is unable to provide a copy or access to the priority document, the applicant will be deemed to have complied if they: request a copy and certificate showing the filing date from the patent office before the deadline to provide a copy; and submit a request that the Commissioner restore the right of priority on the basis of the priority application and a statement indicating that a request for the copy was made to the patent office of the priority application and the date of the request before the deadline to respond to the notice sent under subsection 74(4). When a copy and certificate are provided by the office of filing, the applicant must submit them to the Commissioner not later than three months after they were received by the requester (subsection 74(8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the two-step process: (1) request copy from filing office before deadline; (2) submit restoration request + statement to Commissioner before the notice-deadline. Once obtained from filing office, forward to Commissioner within three months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of priority document — examiner's powers
rubrics_metrics.description: During examination, an examiner may send a notice requiring the applicant to submit a translation of a priority document that is partly or entirely in a language other than English or French. If the examiner has reasonable grounds to believe the translation is not accurate, they may send a further notice requesting: a statement by the translator that, to the best of the translator's knowledge, the translation is accurate; or a new English or French translation, together with a statement by the translator that, to the best of the translator's knowledge, the new translation is accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate, sworn or certified translations when requested; a translator's statement may be required to confirm accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of the right of priority — purpose and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Restoration of the right of priority is a mechanism whereby the time limit for filing an application accompanied by a request for priority is extended beyond the normal twelve-month period after the filing of a priority document. For regular applications filed in Canada and for PCT national phase applications, applicants can request restoration when the filing date of the pending application is more than twelve months after the filing date of the previously regularly filed application, but within two months after the end of those twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration is only available in the narrowly defined two-month window after the 12-month period; check whether your filing date meets the >12 months but within +2 months condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of right of priority — effective date in Canada
rubrics_metrics.description: Restoration of the right of priority is available for patent applications that have a filing date that is on or after October 30, 2019, the coming-into-force date of the Patent Rules (SOR/2019-251).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration rules apply only to filings dated on/after Oct 30, 2019 (except for deemed restoration under PCT rules; see related entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to restore the right of priority — required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: To request restoration under paragraph 28.4(6)(b) of the Patent Act and subsections 77(1) and 77(2) of the Patent Rules, the applicant must, within the relevant prescribed time: make a request for subsection 28.4(6) to apply; state in the request that the failure to file the pending application or co-pending application was unintentional; make a request for priority in the petition or in a document other than the abstract, specification or drawings; and submit to the Commissioner the filing date and the name of the country or office of filing of the previously regularly filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state that the delay was unintentional and include the required priority information in the correct document; missing elements can cause denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period for request for restoration of right of priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The time to make a request to restore the right of priority under subsection 77(1) is: for a regular application (non-PCT) — not later than two months after the filing date of the application or co-pending application; for a PCT national phase application — not later than one month after the national phase entry date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the shorter one-month deadline for PCT national phase restoration requests; compute filing and national phase entry dates precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of priority deemed restored — conditions for Canada (PCT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restoration of the right of priority will be recognized in Canada on the national phase entry date of a PCT national phase application or a divisional resulting from the division of a PCT national phase application under section 162 if: the filing date of the pending application is more than 12 months after the filing date of the previously regularly filed application, but within two months after the end of those 12 months; and if the right of priority was restored under Rule 26bis.3 of the PCT Regulations and that restoration is, under Rule 49ter.1, effective in Canada.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Canadian deemed restoration depends on PCT restoration under specific PCT rules and effective dates; track PCT restoration status closely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed restoration effective in Canada for certain PCT filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The deemed restoration in Canada will be effective for PCT national phase applications with an international filing date that is on or after October 30, 2019, the coming-into-force date of the Patent Rules (SOR/2019-251).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm international filing date and PCT restoration before relying on deemed restoration in Canada.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considered withdrawal of a request for priority — circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for priority will be considered withdrawn under subsections 74(6), 74(9) and 76(3) in the following circumstances: the applicant does not comply with requirement to provide a copy of the priority document or provide access not later than two months after the date of the notice under subsection 74(4); the applicant is considered to have complied but does not submit a copy not later than three months after the day on which it is received (subsection 74(8)); or if the applicant does not provide a translation/new translation or translator statement within four months of the relevant notice under subsection 76(1) or 76(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to notices promptly; failure to comply within the short windows will result in the priority request being deemed withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of a request for priority by applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for priority may be withdrawn by the applicant upon request to the Commissioner. The effective date of the withdrawal of a request for priority is the date on which the request is received by the Commissioner. The withdrawal of priority may have an effect on the claim date, as defined in section 28.1 of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider consequences to claim date before withdrawing priority; ensure Commissioner receives the withdrawal request to fix the effective date.
